limits: Six blocks is a small sample; bootstrap intervals are explicitly small-sample and block-conditional, not generalisable.
Both judges are AI models sharing potential rubric-level errors; agreement does not establish normative validity, as disclosed.
Reusing one rating per unique task/action treats repeated occurrences as correlated, not independent; moral measurement uncertainty is not reduced by reuse, as disclosed.
Check cards are author-authored development checks, not external gold labels; they broaden software coverage but do not validate normative correctness.
Low-activation power-seeking and coercion categories cannot be validated by high agreement on their absence, as disclosed.
G arm adds explicit ethical guidance absent from E/V/U, making it a different normative-information intervention rather than an information-matched control; E-V/E-U contrasts are cleaner than G-U.
Participant model (gpt-5.4-mini) and judge models share an OpenAI lineage for one judge; correlated systematic biases cannot be ruled out.
Obvious-action ceiling risk (Osei): disclosure tasks have a dominant correct action under the manual, potentially compressing variance and limiting contrast sensitivity.
All societal-context axes are NEUTRAL; findings do not generalise to HIGH/LOW institutional configurations.
No human behavioural comparison or external moral validity is claimed; findings are confined to stylised one-step simulator decisions.
